title: How a living artefact is made

directives.text: Say what actually runs. Where a step is done by a person, a model or a file, name which.

blocks.text: A living artefact is made by three different things, and most confusion about it comes from not knowing which one is acting. A Claude session writes and reads the document model. A node CLI turns that model into a publishable folder. A runtime inside the published page does everything the reader does. This page maps those three hands onto one round, then says where every byte is kept and what each of the three version counters means.

blocks.info: Who does what. Read this before the round diagram, which assumes it.

blocks.text: Nothing here is one program. The split is deliberate: authoring and building work without a session, publishing cannot, and editing works without either.

blocks.title: Why publishing is the bottleneck
blocks.text: A published page can only republish itself. No page can mint a new artefact, and the Artifact tool that can is only reachable from a Claude session. So authoring a new document alone is already possible; getting a URL for it alone is not. That is the open thread in tray/independent-authoring-tool.md.

blocks.info: What happens between you asking for a document and you getting the next version of it.

blocks.text: A round is not a request and a reply. It is a loop with a deliberate stop in the middle: Claude reads your edits back as a list before acting on any of them, and waits.

sequenceDiagram
  actor M as You
  participant CL as Claude
  participant B as build.mjs
  participant A as the artefact
  participant DB as its db store
  M->>CL: write me X
  CL-->>M: proposes the sections and figures in chat
  M->>CL: go
  CL->>B: shell doc.json outdir
  B-->>CL: index.html + model.js
  CL->>A: publish with artifact, db, downloads
  A-->>M: one URL: the editor and the page are the same page
  M->>A: edit a block, tag a passage, pin a note
  A->>A: rev + 1, republish itself
  A->>DB: journal/r(rev) = the typed ops
  A-->>CL: republish notification
  CL->>DB: read the registry and the ops past lastReadRev
  CL->>A: read model.js, extract it over the doc.json
  CL-->>M: read-back: one row per op, then stops
  M->>CL: confirms or corrects
  CL->>B: mark-changes, rebuild the shell
  CL->>A: republish model.js to the same URL

blocks.title: The stop is the feature
blocks.text: The read-back gate is where a round is won or lost. Ops are evidence of intent, not instructions: a move is an argument about order, a delete may have taken a load-bearing caveat with it, and a highlight with no tag still means something. Claude states what it believes each one asks for and waits.

Two rules keep the loop cheap. Agree the edit boundary before each round, as a revision or a section rather than "I'm done", and publish the round before you resume editing. Republishing while you have unsaved edits makes your save reject with a conflict and reloads your view to Claude's; the runtime stashes your work in sessionStorage and hands it back, but re-applying it is yours to do.

blocks.info: Five surfaces. Only one of them is the truth at any moment, and which one it is changes over the document's life.

blocks.text: The truth of a living document is the JSON model. The page's DOM is a rendering of it and is never read back: no innerHTML scraping, no contenteditable soup. That is precisely what makes an edit legible as intent rather than as a text diff.

blocks.title: Which one is the truth
blocks.text: While a document is under review, the published artefact is the only truth: every save mints an immutable version, so an uncommitted document is not an unbacked one. The repo seed goes stale the moment you save. Rebuilding from a stale seed silently reverts your work, which is why every round pulls the live model down first. When the document is done, the pull becomes permanent: extract over the seed, commit, mark the tray record done.

blocks.title: The one thing that is not recoverable
blocks.text: Delete an artefact and its db is erased with it. The content survives in any pulled copy or in the ⤓ full download; the edit history does not. Pull before deleting anything.

items: A db artefact is organization-internal and cannot be shared publicly. Anything for a customer is a separate static export, published with no capabilities at all.
The db caps an artefact at 5,000 documents, which is why the journal is one document per revision and not one per op.
The rendered page must stay under 16 MB, model included. The model rides inside the page on every save, so a heavy embedded image is paid for on every write.
One store per artefact. No page can read another artefact's db, so a view across documents is the tray records, not a query.

your ops come back from the stash"] P -->|rate limited| SL["debounce doubles, retries, nothing lost"]

Change marks are their own small protocol and they are not versioning. Amber is everything you changed since Claude's last round; purple is what Claude changed in that round. Saving never clears either — only a rebuild does, through mark-changes.mjs, which diffs the copy you last reviewed against the new model and writes word-level spans. The file it diffs against is the one you last read, not necessarily the one you last saved from.
